idiom_name: scala-logging / SLF4J appender with a chained javax.crypto.Mac
implementation_notes: Scala logging is a facade over the JVM frameworks: scala-logging's LazyLogging/StrictLogging - or org.slf4j directly - provides the chokepoint, while javax.crypto.Mac with a prepared HmacSHA256 supplies the chain. Because JVM projects already carry an SLF4J binding, the hand-written writer is justified only for an audit stream that must be structurally independent of the application log: its own appender, its own sink and its own rotation policy, with the chain state owned by one object.
pitfalls: A Scala object is a per-classloader singleton: under hot reloading, OSGi bundles or several actor systems in one JVM you can end up with two chain heads writing one file.
LazyLogging defers logger creation to first use; initialise the chain state and its key explicitly at startup so no record is written unchained during warm-up.
By-name log arguments (log.info(s"...") interpolators, Scala 3 by-name params) are evaluated on the logging thread - build the canonical record before the call and never interpolate secrets.
